description: Heritage `value of … for key` on a NON-DICT container (here a NUMBER) raises the byte-identical Core `ol-type` the dotted `:n.tom` selector raises: the same `code`, `params` (`expected: "dict"`, `operation: "field"` — the Core selector's spelling, NOT a Heritage `"value of"`), `message`, `stage`, and `severity` (issue #670, slice H5; corrected twin per issue #784). The reader is DICT-ONLY — `spec/data-structures.md:268` types its operand `dictExpr` — so its Core twin is the dotted `.field` selector, not `:n["tom"]`. This fixture previously asserted the `[key]` selector's `expected: "list or dict"`, which reads sensibly for a number but was self-contradictory for a list operand ("index needs a list or dict, but got a list"); the sibling `heritage-value-of-key-*-container-like-core` fixtures now enumerate the remaining non-record container types (word, boolean, list, turtle), and `heritage-value-of-key-record-container-rejected` covers `record` separately because it has no Core twin, so no single sampled type can hide that class again. Proves the reader shares the Core dict-read's type check rather than inventing its own (`spec/conformance.md:146`: alternate spellings only, no new semantics), with NO Heritage spelling in any payload. The span points at the reader's `:n` operand sub-expression, the analog of the selector's own span (localization-only difference — `spec/localization.md`). Heritage depends on Data (`spec/conformance.md:301`), so both `data` and `heritage` are active.
